title: Machine Learning-Based Prediction and Optimization of Heavy Metal Adsorption Performance of Biochar
validation_design: 4:1 train/test split at literature-source level; all rows from one publication assigned exclusively to train or test; preprocessing fitted on training only; 5-fold CV within training
raw_data_status: available from authors on request; published supplement contains optimizer/interface material but not modelling rows
replication_status: published source-aware comparator; independent rerun unavailable
notes: The paper reports q_e train R2=0.99, source-separated test R2=0.99 and 5-fold R2=0.92±0.04. Authors explicitly caution that temporal/feedstock-held-out validation was not performed. Strong source-aware performance therefore exists in at least one contemporary adsorption corpus and must be retained as a counterexample to any universal-collapse claim.

title: Application of random forest regression in modeling the adsorption of methylene blue onto clays
validation_design: conventional random cross-validation versus GroupKFold by source study; no article shared across training and validation folds
replication_status: published independent corroboration; no rerun required for primary matched count
notes: M5 conventional CV R2=0.79 and study-grouped CV R2≈0.66; grouped MAE≈48 and RMSE≈69. The full paper contains 1,098 experiments from 38 studies and reports larger declines/negative grouped R2 for some smaller feature-rich subsets. This is direct prior art for study-aware adsorption validation, so Paper 1 novelty cannot be framed as the first recommendation to use grouped splitting.
